headline: Six straight wins for the Sox as Durbin powers past Chicago
morning_brew: Six games in a row is the kind of streak that makes a man believe again, and I am not saying a damn word about it because I refuse to be the one who jinxes this heater. Caleb Durbin crushed that two-run homer to provide the necessary spark in a tight game, and honestly, it was about damn time someone took charge. It felt like we were waiting all day for a sign, and he stepped up like he had somewhere to be. I haven't seen a team play with this much focus since last season when everything seemed to finally click in the middle of summer.

Patrick Sandoval turned in a gutsy performance, battling through his outing and limiting the damage while the offense searched for a rhythm. The bullpen was lights out behind him, with Aroldis Chapman finally shutting the door in the ninth to preserve the victory. That is the type of team win that makes you forget about the rough start to the month, especially with the way the relievers are attacking the zone lately. For once, the arson squad has actually earned their real name back.

We head to New York to face the Mets next, and the intensity is only gonna ramp up as we stay on the road. My neighbor Rick thinks the schedule makers are conspiring against us in some grand, elaborate plot, but I told him we just need to keep our heads down and play ball. The Duck Boat fund is finally getting a few deposits again, and I plan on keeping it that way by not looking for any excuses while we are cooking.

news_digest.dans_take: The Derby is always a fun watch, though I would prefer to see a Sox slugger taking home the trophy instead of watching the rest of the league showboat.
